title: LoomNativeRelationGraphAndProjectionRegistry
clause: Establish native Surreal relation semantics and an extensible typed domain-source projection registry for Loom.

current_source_discovery: Inspect accepted Surreal schema and all current link/backlink/domain projection symbols.
Discover exact existing plugin/registry conventions before naming extension points.
stop_conditions: Projection identity or ownership is ambiguous.
A proposed relation can widen source access or create a second mutable authority.

scope.summary: Make Loom a typed cross-domain knowledge graph without hard-coding each current or future creative/IDE module. Domain records remain authoritative in their owning Surreal tables; Loom stores typed, attributable, repairable projections and relations.
forbidden_paths: Opaque string-only relation kinds without schema/version validation
Synthetic Loom blocks as substitutes for domain records
Hard-coded CKC, Tailor or Studio-only registry architecture
acceptance_criteria: Native Surreal relation tables represent typed directional edges with stable source, target, project, owner, scope, provenance, relation version and tombstone semantics.
A typed extensible domain-source projection registry declares source kind, source record type, projection builder, repair strategy, supported link/embed actions and version compatibility.
Registering a future publisher requires a typed adapter and fixtures but no Loom schema fork or untyped string dispatch.
Projection creation is idempotent and records the authoritative domain source; deleting or repairing a projection never mutates its domain source.
Backlink and graph APIs return typed relation metadata and reject dangling, cross-project or unauthorized endpoints.
proof_targets: Run native relation create/traverse/tombstone/restart tests against real SurrealDB.
Run registry compatibility, duplicate-registration and unknown-version negative tests.
Run projection repair tests using typed fixture publishers.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend graph foundation; graph and integration UI MTs own Argus proof.

same_project_private_resource_cases: A shared block cannot expose a private source endpoint without an explicit compatible grant.
cross_account_negative_cases: Forged relation IDs and mixed-account endpoints fail closed.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Projection and relation scope is the intersection of all source endpoints.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation removes projection visibility and invalidates traversal caches.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Remote publisher identity is quarantined until explicitly mapped to local scope.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Relation existence, degree and endpoint type are hidden when either endpoint is denied.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.evidence: relation/projection create, repair, deny and delete events
registry compatibility, dangling edge and repair-queue health
projection operation IDs and crash recovery context

risk_if_missed: Every module will invent its own link table or synthetic Loom records, producing brittle duplication and future Tailor/Studio rework.

risks: Registry becomes an untyped service locator.
A projection silently becomes domain authority.

sources: Official SurrealDB record-link and permissions documentation
Handshake Loom and CKC source audit
Typed plugin/adapter patterns in current Handshake
research_provenance.selected_approach: Native typed relations plus a versioned domain-source projection registry with source-authority and repair invariants.
